# Longhorn backend

Atlas discovers Longhorn v1beta2 `nodes` and `volumes` through the Kubernetes API. The same
driver creates, deletes and expands volumes, and creates and deletes snapshots, by writing
`volumes` and `snapshots` in `longhorn.io/v1beta2`. Enable it with `ATLAS_LONGHORN_ENABLE=1`
and, if needed, `ATLAS_LONGHORN_NAMESPACE=longhorn-system`. The gateway service account needs
read access to `nodes`, and get/list/watch/create/update/patch/delete on `volumes` and
`snapshots`. `deploy/k8s/atlas-gateway.yaml` grants that. The gateway fails startup if the
Kubernetes client cannot initialize. Run `POST /api/atlas/v1/backends/bkd_longhorn/discover`
after Longhorn is installed. Failed CRD reads fail discovery; no demo data is substituted.

The backend shows physical node-disk capacity, volume sizes, PVC identity and Longhorn robustness.
Unknown disk capacity is reported as unknown. Its one synthetic `longhorn` pool aggregates disks;
it does not represent a Longhorn replica placement or disk pool. Ceph OSD, CephFS and RGW
operations do not apply.

## Native CRD writes

`create_volume` posts a block `Volume`: size as a byte string, 3 replicas, `blockdev` frontend,
`rwo` unless the request asks for `ReadWriteMany` (`rwx`). The native id is
`longhorn/<namespace>/<name>`, which is what discovery reports for a volume that has no PVC.
`expand_volume` merge-patches `spec.size` and refuses a size that is not larger. `delete_volume`
deletes the Volume; a missing object is success. An id that starts with `pvc/` is refused —
that volume belongs to the PVC path below. `create_snapshot` posts a `Snapshot` with
`spec.volume`, `spec.createSnapshot: true` and the `longhornvolume` label. `delete_snapshot`
deletes it. Clone, backup and replica placement are not implemented.

These calls are unit-tested for the object body and id parsing. They have not been run against
a live Longhorn cluster. Longhorn's admission webhook fills the rest of the Volume spec when
the manager is installed.

`POST /api/atlas/v1/volumes` does not call this path. It still provisions a PVC.

## PVC provisioning

Atlas can create a Longhorn PVC using its Kubernetes job path. Supply both the Atlas backend ID
and a StorageClass whose provisioner is `driver.longhorn.io`:

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "your-tenant-id",
  "name": "app-data",
  "size_bytes": 10737418240,
  "kind": "block",
  "kubernetes": {
    "backend_id": "bkd_longhorn",
    "namespace": "default",
    "storage_class": "longhorn"
  }
}
```

Send this to `POST /api/atlas/v1/volumes` with the usual Atlas authorization. An explicit
Longhorn StorageClass is required: the default policy catalog still resolves to Ceph classes.
Atlas checks the actual StorageClass provisioner and the backend's cordon state before queuing.
Kubernetes VolumeSnapshot, Longhorn backup and replica placement are not implemented by this
driver. Validate RWX migration on your chosen Longhorn storage mode before using it for
KubeVirt live migration.
